- [x] Added an entry in the latest `doc/source/whatsnew/vX.X.X.rst` file if fixing a bug or adding a new feature.

### Problem

`union_indexes` combines `DatetimeIndex` inputs pairwise. When an intermediate union is not contiguous (e.g. `s1 ∪ s3` before `s2` is added), `DatetimeIndex._union` falls back to the generic set path and `_with_freq("infer")`. Inference cannot recover an offset such as `CustomBusinessDay(holidays=...)` from the values, so `freq` becomes `None` and stays `None`, making the result depend on the order of the inputs. The same path is hit by `pd.DataFrame({dict of Series})`.

The bug still reproduces on current `main`; the earlier "not replicable" comment on the issue mistook the `Pandas4Warning` about the default `sort` for the assertion failing.

### Fix

Following the review on the previous attempt (#66295): do not try to preserve `freq` at every pairwise step; validate once at the end. A private helper `_maybe_restore_freq` is called at the two points where the combined index is final (`union_indexes` "special" branch, and after `safe_sort_index` in `_get_combined_index`). It is a no-op unless the result is a monotonic `DatetimeIndex` with `freq is None` and *all* inputs are `DatetimeIndex` sharing the same non-None `freq`; in that case it runs `_validate_frequency` against the final values and re-attaches the `freq` only if they conform. Nothing is inferred, and non-conforming results (e.g. the tz-aware `America/Santiago` DST case from the issue, which has a real gap) keep `freq=None`.

### Test

`test_concat_datetimeindex_freq_order_independent` is parametrized over `sort=True/False/None` (the `None` case also asserts the existing `Pandas4Warning`). Without the fix the `True` and `None` cases fail; with it all three pass. `pandas/tests/indexes`, `frame`, `series`, `reshape`, `resample`, `tseries`, `window`, `groupby` pass locally.
title: BUG: retain DatetimeIndex freq in concat regardless of input order (GH#64253)
